plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment (n=3/3)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 7 columns incl. gene symbol, 6 samples: 3 treated liver vs 3 control liver, unpaired, single batch). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure for a 3-vs-3 unpaired design with no batch: (1) QC on sample structure via blind VST/PCA/distance heatmap to catch outliers or batch-like structure before any test is trusted, (2) minimal count pre-filtering (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model (no external normalization), (4) an explicit-reference-level ~condition design with control as the reference so log2FC is treated-vs-control, (5) a DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, (6) Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering, and, since a knowledge-service check disallowed unconditioned fgsea-on-Hallmark as a first-line enrichment call for this exact situation, (7) an enrichment step built around clusterProfiler GO over-representation (with the tested-gene universe and rrvgo redundancy reduction) as the primary route, with fgsea preranked GSEA (stat-ranked, Hallmark then Reactome) run alongside as the full-ranked-list method and both reported together per the enrichment-agent's judgment of which the significant-gene-count supports. Given n=3 per group, the DE step and the final report explicitly state the power limitation: this design detects only a minority of true DE genes, biased toward large fold changes, and an absent gene from the list is not evidence of no effect. Reference gene sets used: MSigDB Hallmark (human), Reactome pathways, WikiPathways (human), and MSigDB GO-BP for the ORA route — all confirmed present in this environment. No batch correction is applied (single batch, none declared).

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap
Keep gene with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (3)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways/GO
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (full ranked gene list, not thresholded), MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (full ranked gene list, not thresholded), MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
